Subject: RTO/RPO acceptance criteria for multi-region switchover

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinTrust is keen to finalize the resilience annex for our contract. Two quick asks from our ops/security teams:

- Can Redwood provide a written acceptance criteria for a primary->secondary regional switchover (warm standby) that specifies what you measure for RTO and RPO during an on-call switchover?
- For a subset of our payment-processing flows (low-latency, high-consistency), we need a temporary variance request: target RTO <= 15 minutes and RPO <= 5 minutes for the production cutover validation window.

We attached our questionnaire and a list of flows. We know these are tight numbers; if there are constraints (e.g., cache warm-up, model cold starts, or cross-region replication lag), please call them out along with any mitigations.

Can we aim for a short working session this week to align on acceptance test steps, metrics to collect, and any carveouts that we should include in the SLA addendum?

Ana — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. We ran this with Product and Infra; below is a proposed starting point for acceptance criteria and a short list of temporary variance options.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Test type: Controlled canary switchover (production traffic sampling at 2%)
- RTO measurement: time from switchover trigger to first successful end-to-end request at production SLA levels (p95 latency within agreed bound)
- RPO measurement: record-level replication lag as measured by the replication stream commit timestamp versus primary commit time (target window measured in seconds/minutes)
- Required telemetry: end-to-end request traces, token-level latency histograms, KV cache hit-rate and warm-up time, replication commit timestamps
- Rollback criteria: automatic rollback if error rate > 2% or p95 latency degrades > 50% for > 5 minutes

Temporary variance proposal (to address FinTrust request):
- Payment-processing flows (scope list from your questionnaire): temporary RTO target = 20 minutes, RPO target = 10 minutes for the validated cutover window (we can discuss tightening after runbook and canary passes)
- Rationale: warm-up of model and KV caches in secondary region plus shard rebalancing can add measurable latency; 15/5 is achievable with dedicated pre-warm steps but requires reserved capacity and an acceptance test window.

Next steps:
1) Align on exact scope of flows (please confirm the list in the questionnaire).
2) Infra-led runbook / pre-warm checklist (Grace will propose).
3) Sign-off on temporary variance term and schedule an acceptance test (Marissa will coordinate legal/ops items).

If this looks reasonable I can schedule a 45-minute alignment tomorrow afternoon.

—Ben

Ben — adding a few technical constraints and what we'll need from FinTrust to make the variance safe to sign: 

Quoted from Ben's message:
> - Required telemetry: end-to-end request traces, token-level latency histograms, KV cache hit-rate and warm-up time, replication commit timestamps

Notes from Infra:
- Replication: we need confirmation of the DB commit timestamp availability (CDC stream) for the listed flows. Without CDC or write-timestamp, our RPO estimate is a best-effort approximation.
- Cache warm-up: model KV cache and embedding caches can take 5–12 minutes depending on working set size; pre-warm scripts should be run as part of the acceptance window.
- Capacity: to meet a stricter RTO of <=15 minutes we recommend a reserved Dedicated capacity pool during the acceptance test window (to avoid cold allocation delays). This can be scoped to specific model shards.
- Observability hooks: FinTrust must provide access to a read-only Prometheus endpoint or agree to push required metrics to our secure telemetry ingestion for the test window.

I'll draft a short runbook checklist (pre-warm, traffic ramp, canary thresholds, rollback steps) and share for review.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ana — looping in legal to flag the temporary variance clause and acceptance-test sign-off flow. Ben/Grace, I've attached a runbook-checklist and an acceptance criteria table with the conditional variance language. Key commercial points from Legal/Ops: 

- Variance duration: a time-boxed validation window (recommended: 14 days max) after which metrics must meet the agreed targets for at least 3 consecutive canary runs or the variance lapses.
- Liability carveouts: we enumerate third-party outages and cross-region network partitions; FinTrust must approve the carveout language for any dependent vendor.
- Sign-off: the canonical sign-off requires an SRE-approved runbook test report (Infra), an ops tsque (FinTrust) sign-off on observed metrics, and countersignature from Redwood Legal.

Please review the attached checklist and the table; if FinTrust accepts the conditional variance language, we can prepare a short addendum and a DocuSign packet. Can we target signatures by EOD Friday next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
